grades.question: A Spirit chooses Growth with two Add Presence actions. May the second placement use the first as its range origin? Which Presence-track disks may be taken, and how do uncovered Energy/Card Plays numbers combine?

expected.answer: Yes; resolve Growth actions in chosen order, so the first placement can extend the second. Each placement takes the leftmost remaining Presence from either chosen track. Use only the highest uncovered Energy number and highest uncovered Card Plays number, not their sum.

requested_parts: whether the second Add Presence can use the first placement as its range origin
which track disks may be taken
how Energy and Card Plays track numbers combine
observed.answer: Yes. Resolve multiple Add Presence placements sequentially, so the first new disk can be the origin for the second. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track for each placement. Energy/Turn and Card Plays are separate tracks: use the highest uncovered value on each, and do not add uncovered numbers together.

evidence.text: - **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

**Gain Energy:** Take Energy equal to the **highest uncovered number** on your Energy/Turn track. Energy/Turn and Card Plays each use their own **highest uncovered value**; neither track adds its uncovered numbers together. Unspent Energy carries over between turns; it is individual and cannot ordinarily be transferred to another Spirit.

grades.question: In a Ravage a land has one Town, one Explorer and two undamaged Dahan, with no Defend or prior Blight. Resolve damage to land, Dahan, surviving counterattack and resulting Fear if the players destroy the Town.

expected.answer: Invaders do 3 Damage simultaneously to land and Dahan, adding one Blight, killing one Dahan and damaging the other by 1. The surviving Dahan still deals 2 Damage, destroying the Town and generating 1 Fear. Dahan do not absorb/prevent land damage; partial Dahan damage clears at Time Passes.

requested_parts: Ravage Damage to land and Blight result
Ravage Damage to Dahan and survivors
surviving Dahan counterattack and Fear if the Town is destroyed
observed.answer: The Town and Explorer deal 3 total Damage to the land and, separately, 3 to the Dahan. The land takes at least 2, so add one Blight. Two Dahan Damage kills one Dahan and leaves the other with 1 marked Damage. The surviving Dahan counterattacks for 2 Damage and can destroy the Town; that destruction earns 1 Fear.

evidence.text: Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. Damage already marked on a piece does not reduce its outgoing Damage. Invaders deal the resulting Damage **equally, separately and simultaneously** to the land and its Dahan:

- **Dahan:** Every 2 Damage kills one Dahan; allocate efficiently to kill as many as possible, rather than spreading damage to keep all alive. If 1 remains after that, mark one surviving Dahan with 1 Damage. Return destroyed Dahan to supply.

Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. Do not add the setup +1 again. [FAQ .9v5kfqt]

grades.question: Explain how Elements apply to multiple thresholds and multiple Powers. May an innate be used twice with twice the Elements, may its levels use different lands, and how does an “Instead” level work?

expected.answer: Elements are checked, not spent, so may meet any number of Powers/thresholds. An innate is normally one use, regardless of surplus Elements. Use all met levels top to bottom on one target, with Instead replacing previous effects. May pretend to have fewer Elements for the entire Power, not cherry-pick levels.

whether an Innate can be used twice
whether levels may target different lands
Instead level effect
observed.answer: Elements are checked and never spent, so the same Elements can meet multiple Powers and thresholds. An ordinary Innate is used once per turn, not twice merely because its Elements are doubled, and all levels apply to the same target land or Spirit. An “Instead” level replaces prior effects rather than adding to them.

evidence.text: An Innate is available each turn when its Element requirements are met; ordinarily it costs no Energy and uses no Card Play. Elements are **checked, never spent**. The same Elements can satisfy multiple Powers and thresholds. Gain a card's Elements as soon as it is played, whether or not its text is used, and lose them as soon as it leaves play.

- Unless explicitly different, use **one target land or Spirit, once per turn**. Multiple effects and all innate levels apply to that same target. You cannot pay twice for an ordinary card use or use an innate twice just by having twice its Elements.

- Resolve the base effect and every met threshold in printed order **unless explicit timing text says otherwise**: “First” and “Before” can place a threshold instruction ahead of earlier-printed base instructions. A level saying **Instead** replaces previous effects rather than adding to them. You may treat yourself as having fewer Elements **for the whole Power**, consistently, rather than selecting individual thresholds to omit.

grades.question: A legal target lacks pieces needed for one printed instruction. May the Power still be used? May the player choose individual unwanted instructions to skip, or forego the whole Power and recover its Energy?

expected.answer: May use it; perform instructions in order, skipping impossible parts and doing the rest. Cannot skip possible mandatory instructions at will (apart from permitted choices, up-to, or selecting fewer Elements consistently). May forego the whole Power; no Energy refund, and played-card Elements remain while in play.

requested_parts: whether Power may be used when one instruction cannot be performed
whether possible instructions may be arbitrarily skipped
whether foregoing Power refunds Energy
observed.answer: Yes, a Power can be used on an otherwise legal target even if one instruction cannot be performed; resolve in printed order and do as much as possible. Once started, the player cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction. The whole Power may be foregone, but the played card’s Energy is not refunded.

evidence.text: - Resolve instructions in printed order, doing as much as possible. Inability to perform one instruction does not prohibit playing or using a Power on an otherwise legal target. Target restrictions are in its target bar, not implied by its text. You may even target a land where the effects accomplish nothing, but must actually attempt the text to count as using/targeting the Power.

- You may forego the whole Power, but cannot arbitrarily omit a possible mandatory instruction after starting. “Up to” allows zero. “Or” chooses between its adjoining clauses, not other separate text on the card. Choose the branch **before resolving either option**; you cannot start one to inspect its results and then switch to the other. [FAQ .9v5kcmx]

Use Fast Power Cards in play and eligible Fast Innates. Players choose their order; finish one Power before starting another. A Power cannot interrupt another Power. You may forego a Power entirely, retaining a played card's Elements but receiving no Energy refund. A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow: use it now or forego it.

grades.question: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?

expected.answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated. An outright Destroy instruction eliminates its specified piece regardless of its Damage or Health. Remove likewise takes the specified piece off the board without requiring Damage to reach Health. Replace removes the original and puts the specified replacement in its place.

observed.answer: Normal Power Damage marks Invaders and can accumulate with Damage from separate Powers and counterattacks within a turn; it normally does not harm Dahan or land. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. evidence.text: **Gather N:** Move N of the specified pieces from adjacent land(s) into the target land. **Push N:** Move N from the target to adjacent land(s). requested_parts: number of Thunderspeaker Presence accompanying two moved Dahan
whether Presence can accompany them into Ocean made legal by Ocean
observed.answer: Thunderspeaker may accompany each moved Dahan with Presence, so two Dahan can carry two Presence. Other Spirits’ Presence may end up in Ocean through a legal Power when Ocean’s rule makes it a land.

evidence.text: - **Thunderspeaker:** Presence may accompany each moved Dahan, including generic Move as well as Gather/Push; two Dahan can carry two Presence. **Sworn to Victory** triggers after an entire single-land Ravage for each Dahan destroyed there: destroy one of Thunderspeaker's Presence within Range 1 per Dahan, even if no Blight was added. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. evidence.text:
## Setup

**Deck preparation includes randomization, not just selecting counts:** shuffle all Fear Cards before taking the nine used cards; shuffle each Invader stage separately before removing its unseen unused card and stacking the stages.

1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides into the island. For one Spirit use one board. For two, any fitting arrangement is legal; the rulebook illustrates bottom-to-bottom with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.

2. **Invader deck:** Shuffle each stage separately. Remove one card of each stage unseen. Stack **3 Stage I cards on top, 4 Stage II below them, 5 Stage III at the bottom**. Put this 12-card deck in Explore.

3. **Fear:** Put **4 Fear markers per Spirit** in the Fear Pool. Shuffle the 15 Fear Cards and use 9 unseen: three cards, Terror II divider, three cards, Terror III divider, three cards, from top to bottom. Start at Terror I. Leave space for Earned Fear Cards and Fear discard.

4. **Blight:** Randomly select a Blight Card, Healthy Island side up; do not inspect its reverse. Put **2 Blight per Spirit plus exactly 1 additional Blight total** on it. This is the official initial-pool correction. The additional 1 is applied only at setup, never again on a card flip. Remaining box Blight is separate from this pool.

5. **Supply:** Shuffle Minor and Major decks separately, each with its own discard. Make Invaders, Dahan and Energy available to everyone.

6. **Spirits:** Each player takes one color's 13 Presence and reminder markers (any accidental extra disk is a spare, not additional Presence for play), a different Spirit panel, and that Spirit's four Unique cards as their starting hand. Each starts on a different Island Board and follows the back-of-panel setup exactly. Where several choices equally satisfy setup, choose freely; separate Presence-placement instructions may use the same land. Put remaining disks on the dashed spaces of both Presence tracks; the leftmost solid starting spaces remain uncovered. Starting boards do not restrict where a Spirit can act after setup.

7. **Initial Explore:** Reveal the top Invader card and Explore normally. Then put it face-up in **Build**. This Explore is the last part of setup; Ravage starts empty. The first actual turn begins with the Spirit Phase.

**Introductory alternatives (CORE p.3):** Choose a low-complexity Spirit: Lightning's Swift Strike, Vital Strength of the Earth, River Surges in Sunlight, or Shadows Flicker Like Flame. A new player may use its Power Progression: remove the listed Minor and Major cards from the shared decks and reserve them; on gaining a Power, take the next one into hand instead of drawing four. Gaining a Major still requires Forgetting a card. If everyone is new, omit the Blight Card and use the printed board pool: **5 Blight per Spirit +1 total** at setup, losing if it empties; there is no flip or ongoing Blighted effect. Do not use an Adversary or Scenario. Progressions are a teaching aid, not compulsory for low-complexity Spirits.

grades.question: Ocean In Play is active on a board. Infinite Vitality with its threshold protects Dahan in that Ocean, and a Power Pushes a Dahan into it. Ocean In Play triggers but cannot destroy that Dahan. With an adjacent non-Ocean land available, what happens next: does the Dahan remain until cleanup, or is it Pushed? Is that relocation an actual Push within the triggered action or merely cleanup?

expected.answer: Ocean In Play Pushes the surviving Dahan to a non-Ocean land as part of its own triggered action. This is an actual Push, capable of triggering applicable movement effects; it is not the later non-action cleanup operation. Cleanup only handles a piece still illegally placed after the action tree. No expansion effect or piece is needed for this branch: the FAQ expressly supplies Infinite Vitality threshold on the Ocean as a core-game case.

requested_parts: result for Dahan pushed into Ocean but protected from Drowning
whether relocation is a Push within triggered action or later cleanup
observed.answer: Infinite Vitality prevents Drowning from destroying the Dahan, so it cannot remain in Ocean between action trees. With a legal adjacent non-Ocean land, the Dahan is Pushed there within the action; that is an actual Push and may trigger applicable movement effects, not cleanup.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. grades.question: Spirit A has an existing +2 bonus to its Power Ranges and uses Reaching Grasp, whose text grants target Spirit B +2 Range with all their Powers. Does A’s existing bonus increase the amount granted to +4, or does B receive +2? Does B’s Power-only bonus cover Innate Powers as well as Power Cards, and can it extend ordinary Growth placement?

expected.answer: The grant stays +2; Range boosts do not increase another Range boost. Reaching Grasp’s Power-only bonus applies to B’s Powers, including Innates and Power Cards, subject to the normal Range-arrow restrictions. It does not extend ordinary Growth, which is not a Power; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth.

requested_parts: whether A’s +2 increases Reaching Grasp’s granted +2
whether B’s Power-only boost applies to Innates

observed.answer: A’s existing +2 does not increase Reaching Grasp’s printed +2 bonus; B receives +2 Range. A Power Range bonus applies to B’s Power Cards and Innates, but does not extend Growth placement.

evidence.text: - **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. grades.question: A Spirit plays and pays for a Power Card, then foregoes its entire text because it has no legal target or the Spirit chooses not to use it. With no other effect removing the card, do its printed Elements remain available for Innates, is its Energy refunded, and does the card leave play immediately or during Time Passes?

expected.answer: Its printed Elements remain while the card is in play and can support Innates even though its text was not used. The paid Energy is not refunded. Foregoing the text does not remove/discard the card immediately; it stays in play and is normally discarded during Time Passes, when its Elements go away.
source_refs: CORE p.17 General Principle You Can Skip Using A Power’s Effect; pp.8,10,16

requested_parts: whether played card Elements remain after foregone text
whether Energy refunded
when card leaves play
observed.answer: Yes, its printed Elements remain available while the card is in play. No Energy is refunded. The card remains in play through its phase and is discarded at Time Passes.

evidence.text: Use Fast Power Cards in play and eligible Fast Innates. Players choose their order; finish one Power before starting another. A Power cannot interrupt another Power. You may forego a Power entirely, retaining a played card's Elements but receiving no Energy refund. A Fast Power cannot be saved for Slow: use it now or forego it.

Discard played cards to each owner's **personal discard**. All Damage on surviving Invaders and Dahan clears, Elements from cards go away, and single-turn effects expire; remove reminder markers. Unused Energy remains. Permanent board changes, such as moved pieces, destroyed pieces, removed Blight and earned Fear, remain. Printed track Elements remain while uncovered.

grades.question: Two separate Ravages occur in the same land before Time Passes. Each would deal 4 Damage before the land’s Defend 3; assume that pre-Defend total stays 4, and one Dahan starts healthy. Is Defend expended on the first Ravage? How much Damage reaches land and Dahan each time? Do the two 1-Damage land results combine into Blight, and what happens to that Dahan on the second Ravage?

expected.answer: Defend is not expended: it reduces each Ravage by 3 for the entire turn. Each deals 1 Damage to land and 1 to Dahan. Land Damage below 2 is ignored per occurrence, so the two 1-Damage land results never combine into Blight. The Dahan’s first 1 Damage persists until Time Passes; the second 1 reaches its 2 Health and destroys it before a second counterattack.

requested_parts: whether Defend is spent on first Ravage
land and Dahan Damage in each Ravage
whether separate 1 Damage land outcomes combine into Blight
effect of second Ravage on previously damaged Dahan
observed.answer: Defend is not expended; each occurrence receives Defend 3. Each 4-Damage Ravage therefore deals 1 to the land and separately 1 to Dahan. One Damage to land does nothing and is not saved, so the two Ravages do not combine to add Blight. The first Ravage marks 1 Damage on the healthy Dahan; the second adds another and destroys it.

evidence.text: **Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. Protected surviving Dahan then counterattack normally. It does not protect them from direct Destroy instructions or Damage from other sources. [FAQ .7w4g8nu; original card text]

- **Land:** If it takes **2 or more Damage**, add **one Blight**, regardless of how much more than 2. One Damage to land does nothing and is not saved for another action. Resolve Blight/Presence loss and cascading as described below.

- **Dahan:** Every 2 Damage kills one Dahan; allocate efficiently to kill as many as possible, rather than spreading damage to keep all alive. If 1 remains after that, mark one surviving Dahan with 1 Damage. Return destroyed Dahan to supply.

grades.question: What is the required order of an individual Spirit's Growth, normal track Energy gain, and actual playing/paying for Power Cards? May the Spirit take its normal Energy income before finishing Growth or actually play/pay before Growth? expected.answer: The Spirit must complete Growth, then gain normal Energy, then play and pay for Power Cards. It may not take the normal income or actually play/pay cards before Growth. The normal income step follows Growth and uses the highest number then uncovered, including a higher number just revealed by that Growth, so the benefit applies in this same Spirit Phase. grades.question: A Spirit still has Presence disks on its Presence tracks. When resolving an ordinary Add Presence instruction, may it choose to reposition one of its Presence already on the island instead of taking a track disk, or is repositioning permitted only after its tracks are empty?

requested_parts: whether Add Presence may reposition island Presence while track disks remain
observed.answer: Yes. An Add Presence instruction may reposition any of the Spirit’s island Presence even while track disks remain.

evidence.text: - **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. grades.question: Wrap in Wings of Sunlight meets its threshold. Its target land initially has no Dahan, but Dahan are available in adjacent lands. expected.answer: Wrap’s explicit First instruction Gathers before the base Move, allowing those gathered Dahan to be moved by the base effect and Defend 5 in the destination if at least one moves. Dissolve’s explicit Before Pushing instruction resolves its threshold Damage before the Explorer Push (after the preceding replacements). whether Dissolve damage happens before Explorer Push

evidence.text: - **Location-dependent effects:** **Wrap in Wings of Sunlight** resolves its threshold’s **First, Gather up to 3 Dahan** before its base Move; those gathered Dahan may then move and allow the destination’s Defend. evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. Humans cannot stay there between action trees: if Drowning fails, Push survivors to non-Ocean lands within that action. This is an actual Push and can trigger applicable movement effects, unlike later cleanup. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. Remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land afterward. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. grades.question: Spirit A has an existing +2 bonus to its Power Ranges and uses Reaching Grasp, whose text grants target Spirit B +2 Range with all their Powers. Does A’s existing bonus increase the amount granted to +4, or does B receive +2? Does B’s Power-only bonus cover Innate Powers as well as Power Cards, and can it extend ordinary Growth placement?

expected.answer: The grant stays +2; Range boosts do not increase another Range boost. Reaching Grasp’s Power-only bonus applies to B’s Powers, including Innates and Power Cards, subject to the normal Range-arrow restrictions. It does not extend ordinary Growth, which is not a Power; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth.

requested_parts: Whether A’s range bonus enlarges Reaching Grasp grant
Whether B bonus applies to Innates
Whether Power-only bonus applies to Growth
observed.answer: A’s existing +2 does not increase Reaching Grasp’s printed +2 grant; B receives +2. A Power Range bonus applies to B’s Powers, including Innates, but does not extend ordinary Growth.

evidence.text: - **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. grades.question: Two separate Ravages occur in the same land before Time Passes. Each would deal 4 Damage before the land’s Defend 3; assume that pre-Defend total stays 4, and one Dahan starts healthy. Is Defend expended on the first Ravage? How much Damage reaches land and Dahan each time? Do the two 1-Damage land results combine into Blight, and what happens to that Dahan on the second Ravage?

expected.answer: Defend is not expended: it reduces each Ravage by 3 for the entire turn. Each deals 1 Damage to land and 1 to Dahan. Land Damage below 2 is ignored per occurrence, so the two 1-Damage land results never combine into Blight. The Dahan’s first 1 Damage persists until Time Passes; the second 1 reaches its 2 Health and destroys it before a second counterattack.

requested_parts: Whether Defend expended and per-Ravage damage
Whether land Damage accumulates into Blight
Dahan on second Ravage
observed.answer: Defend is not expended: each Ravage separately reduces 4 by Defend 3, so 1 Damage reaches land and 1 reaches Dahan each time. The two one-point land results do not combine; each Ravage’s 1 Damage does nothing to the land. The Dahan takes 1 each time and is destroyed on the second Ravage when its marked Damage reaches 2 Health.

evidence.text: **Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. Protected surviving Dahan then counterattack normally. It does not protect them from direct Destroy instructions or Damage from other sources. [FAQ .7w4g8nu; original card text]

- **Land:** If it takes **2 or more Damage**, add **one Blight**, regardless of how much more than 2. One Damage to land does nothing and is not saved for another action. Resolve Blight/Presence loss and cascading as described below.

grades.question: Wrap in Wings of Sunlight meets its threshold. Its target land initially has no Dahan, but Dahan are available in adjacent lands. Does its threshold’s “First, Gather up to 3 Dahan” happen before the base Move, so those Dahan can then be moved and the destination Defended, or must the base Move finish first because it is printed higher? Likewise, with Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship’s threshold, does its Invader-on-Invader Damage happen before or after Pushing the Explorers?

expected.answer: Wrap’s explicit First instruction Gathers before the base Move, allowing those gathered Dahan to be moved by the base effect and Defend 5 in the destination if at least one moves. Dissolve’s explicit Before Pushing instruction resolves its threshold Damage before the Explorer Push (after the preceding replacements). Such timing words override the default top-to-bottom position; they do not create another Power use.
source_refs: threshold First instruction and base Move/Defend

requested_parts: Wrap threshold First/Gather timing
Dissolve threshold damage versus Explorer Push
observed.answer: Wrap’s “First, Gather up to 3 Dahan” occurs before its base Move, so those Dahan can move and allow destination Defend. Dissolve’s Invaders-damage-each-other instruction occurs simultaneously before the Explorer Push.

evidence.text: - **Location-dependent effects:** **Wrap in Wings of Sunlight** resolves its threshold’s **First, Gather up to 3 Dahan** before its base Move; those gathered Dahan may then move and allow the destination’s Defend. It grants no Defend if zero Dahan move: there is no moved-to land. Moving Dahan to their original land can count as Move if the Power permits. **Blazing Renewal** permits its target Spirit to add its destroyed Presence directly to one legal island land, not to tracks. Its printed “adds 2” is mandatory to the extent possible, using the Power user's Presence for its internal Range; it cannot deal threshold Damage with no destroyed Presence restored: “that land” refers to where it adds Presence. **The Trees and Stones Speak of War** deals 1 Damage per Dahan and grants Defend 2 per Dahan in its target land. Its threshold moves Defend 2 with each Dahan it Pushes, leaving the remaining Defend in the target. Only this Power's Defend 2 per pushed Dahan travels; separate Defend from another effect, such as Words of Warning, stays in its original land. A later Power moving those Dahan does not carry that Defend. [Core: .9v5kfqd, .9v5kfr0, .bu6oc8n, .bu6ocxq]

- **Core Power specifics:** **Song of Sanctity** is Slow, despite missing cost-circle ink in some printings. Its Explorer condition selects its effect: with Explorers, Push all of them; otherwise remove 1 Blight. This is not a free choice to remove Blight while Explorers remain. **Dissolve the Bonds of Kinship** line 3 Pushes all Explorers **to as many different lands as possible**, using every available legal destination up to the number of Explorers; its Invaders damaging each other do so simultaneously, **before** the Explorer Push as the threshold specifies. **Poisoned Land**'s threshold counts the Blight that its own earlier instruction added. **Tsunami**'s threshold adds Fear for each other Coastal land it affects. source_refs: /home/jonny/projects/boardgame-rules/docs/quality/summary-qa/spirit-island/2026-11-05-batch-002957/card-scope-source/vengeance_of_the_dead.jpg | all printed rules text in lower half; for Fear cards all three Terror panels | SHA256 76c73c2c5da794ee77a565368e88cae8a9a29b3863bb579f2131f1eaed4fe22f

requested_parts: Threshold Damage in adjacent lands
Effect on target land
observed.answer: Yes. The threshold may send its Damage into adjacent lands; the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers Vengeance.

evidence.text: - **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Separately repeated instances can trigger one another, but neither can recur within its own chain. **Vengeance of the Dead** uses this timing; its corrected base text grants 3 Fear and, after an effect destroys Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, deals 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction. [Core: what-items-are-triggered-actions, .bu6oc8x, .7w4gdth, .7w4gdtj]

If a transferred Unique references a special effect defined by a Spirit's rule, such as Drown, that definition still applies; skip instructions requiring a personal track you do not have. expected.answer: Yes. To use a Repeat granted by Powerstorm, the target Spirit pays that repeated Power Card’s cost again. The same payment condition applies to each further Repeat granted by the threshold.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

evidence.text: Fear effects are not Spirit Powers. A Spread of Rampant Green has three Presence in that land and uses Choke the Land with Green to skip its Ravage, destroying one of those Presence. No other effect changes the land before Build. expected.answer: The first payment skips only the Ravage. For the later Build, Green makes a fresh optional choice and must destroy another of its own Presence in that land to skip it. observed.answer: No. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once, even if it is moved and damaged again later in that use.

evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions.
